claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure containing distinct grain-boundary networks, phase interfaces, or defect distributions.
A multiscale model coupled to a machine-learning surrogate can predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior of HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed framework will outperform conventional full-scale simulations in predictive accuracy and speed.
Local mechanical responses associated with hierarchical features can be extracted using short-timescale simulations or experiments.
A machine-learning surrogate calibrated on local microstructural responses can predict global mechanical properties.
Temperature and strain rate influence mechanical properties and dislocation-mediated plastic deformation in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed tensile and fracture conditions will activate dislocation-nucleation sites and grain-boundary effects in HfNbTiVAl10.
The hierarchical heterostructure mediates local stress concentrations and plastic-deformation mechanisms.
Characterizing local stress and plastic-deformation responses supplies sufficient inputs for accurate prediction of macroscopic mechanical behavior.
Localized plasticity is a salient contribution to mechanical response in compositionally complex alloys.
Isolating microstructural contributions to plasticity and damage allows the integrated model to bypass computationally intensive full-scale simulations.
Bypassing full-scale simulations will accelerate prediction while maintaining or improving accuracy.
The proposed model will reduce prediction time by at least a factor of ten.
The proposed model will reduce prediction error for Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness by approximately 20–30% relative to established full-scale simulations.
Conventional full-scale molecular-dynamics or continuum simulations require extensive computation to capture the hierarchical structure.
Unmodeled defect interactions or secondary phase transitions may cause the surrogate to fail.
An insufficient or unrepresentative training dataset may lead to errors in predicting complex nonlinear behavior.
Failure to reach the specified speed and accuracy gains, or systematic disagreement with independent measurements beyond predicted error margins, is predeclared as falsifying evidence.
